papers.title: Does Global Slowing Explain Age Effects in Inhibitory Control?
papers.reason: This directly concerns age-related changes in inhibitory control, an executive function, though it appears primarily behavioural rather than computational.

papers.title: Modeling decision dynamics disentangles working memory, cognitive control and reinforcement learning and reveals clinical differences
papers.reason: This is a central computational modelling paper on working memory, cognitive control, reinforcement learning, decision dynamics, and clinical phenotyping.

papers.title: Task-specific theta enhancement and domain-general alpha/beta suppression as oscillatory signatures of cognitive flexibility
papers.reason: This reports oscillatory EEG signatures of cognitive flexibility, a core executive-control construct directly relevant to computational models.

papers.title: Ventral striatal and caudate contributions to episodic retrieval.
papers.reason: This focuses on episodic retrieval rather than planning, working memory, attention, cognitive control, or executive-function assessment.

papers.title: Frustrative nonreward engages midfrontal theta power and modulates effort expenditure.
papers.reason: This links midfrontal theta to effort expenditure after frustrative nonreward, providing neural evidence relevant to cognitive control and motivated decision making.

papers.title: EARLY-LIFE STRESS INDUCES SEXUALLY DIMORPHIC BRAIN AGING VIA MESOLIMBIC ALTERATIONS AND FRONTO-STRIATAL DYSFUNCTION
papers.reason: This addresses fronto-striatal dysfunction and brain aging, but the executive-function link is broad and indirect from the title alone.

papers.title: Associations Between Resting-State EEG Delta-band Activity at Selected Parietal Electrodes and Cognitive Changes Following Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation in Patients with Mild Cognitive Impairment: An Exploratory Analysis.
papers.reason: This is relevant to EEG-based cognitive monitoring in mild cognitive impairment, but it is exploratory and not specifically focused on executive-function modelling or task-based classification.
